subject: Re: SIG follow-up — encryption & key custody clarifications
message_1_body:
Hi Vanessa and team,

Thanks for the initial SIG submission earlier this week. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups specifically around encryption controls — both in transit and at rest — and a few asks on key custody and rotation for the customer-facing environment. I attached the subset of SIG rows we want to confirm (acme-sig-questions.xlsx).

High level asks: we need a plain-English description of how keys are provisioned and who has administrative access; a sample CloudTrail entry showing a KMS key usage event; confirmation on whether keys used for customer data are backed by an HSM (and if so, vendor/model); and your key rotation cadence and automation details.

Can you respond with the relevant artifacts or links by EOD Wednesday (Acme PDT)? Our procurement team is gating the SOC/SIG packet on this.

Thanks —
Paul
Paul Dunne
Security Manager, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachment: acme-sig-questions.xlsx (Excel — selected SIG rows)
message_2_body:
Paul — thanks for the clear list. We can provide what you asked for. Quick summary up front, with artifacts attached and links to a small evidence bundle: 

- In transit: All customer traffic to Redwood hosted APIs is TLS1.2+ with modern cipher suites; internal service-to-service connections in the public hosted environment use mTLS for control-plane calls. We will attach an excerpt from our TLS config and a sample packet trace redacted for PII.

- At rest & KMS: Customer data at rest is encrypted using per-tenant data keys that are envelope-encrypted with a master key stored in a customer-isolated AWS KMS (for Hosted customers we use Redwood-managed KMS keys in the Redwood account unless the customer requests dedicated keys). Keys are configured with key policies limiting who can use or administer them; a short excerpt is attached.

- HSM: For Dedicated and Private deployments we offer HSM-backed key storage (AWS CloudHSM or customer-provided HSM). For our hosted default, keys are AWS KMS (multi-tenant within legal constructs) which uses FIPS 140-2 validated modules. If you need the HSM model used by a specific Dedicated instance, we can provide the appliance details.

- Rotation & automation: Root/master KEKs are rotated on a 12-month schedule by default; intermediate/data keys are rotated automatically per workload and on-demand via our orchestration layer (typical automatic rotation window 90 days for short-lived DEKs; KEK rotation is incremental to avoid service disruption). We will attach our KMS rotation playbook (redwood-kms-rotation-plan.pdf) and a sample CloudTrail event where a CMK was used to decrypt a data key (cloudtrail-sample.log).

I'll attach: redwood-sig-encryption-responses.pdf (answers & mappings to your SIG rows), kms-policies-excerpt.txt, and cloudtrail-sample.log. If you need an HSM attestation package for an on-prem Dedicated plan, let me know and I'll loop in Compliance.

Next step: I'll send a short internal note to Marissa and Jonas to grab the rotation plan and the DocuSign link for our standard evidence transfer.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sig-encryption-responses.pdf; kms-policies-excerpt.txt; cloudtrail-sample.log

message_4_subject: SIG evidence — encryption controls and custody (Acme)
message_4_body:
Paul — following up with the finalized evidence bundle and a couple clarifications per your asks. Summary of what we're sharing and how to interpret it: 

1) Key provisioning & access: Data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant and are never persisted in plaintext. DEKs are envelope-encrypted using a Customer Master Key (CMK) in AWS KMS. For Hosted customers the CMKs are Redwood-managed in our KMS account; the key policy explicitly restricts Decrypt/Encrypt to a service principal representing the Redwood runtime (policy excerpt attached: kms-policies-excerpt.txt). Customers on Dedicated/Private can supply their own CMKs (BYOK) or opt into CloudHSM-backed KMS where the HSM module provides FIPS-validated key storage.

2) HSM specifics: For Dedicated CloudHSM pools we use AWS CloudHSM v4 appliances (model: Luna/Nitro-backed cluster) for customers who opt in. For fully on-prem air-gapped deployments we support Thales Luna HSMs — we can provide firmware and attestation artifacts under NDA.

3) Rotation cadence and automation: Operational defaults: DEKs rotated per workload on a 90-day cadence via our orchestration layer; CMK (KEK) rotations performed 12 months with key material staged and rolled using a non-disruptive key rewrap workflow. Rotation is automated where the KMS supports it; our rotation playbook (redwood-kms-rotation-plan.pdf) describes the steps, escalation paths, and rollback procedure.

4) Evidence links: We've uploaded a small evidence bundle to a shared Drive folder (link below). The bundle includes: (a) redwood-sig-encryption-responses.pdf (SIG row-by-row answers), (b) kms-policies-excerpt.txt, (c) cloudtrail-sample.log (redacted), and (d) redwood-kms-rotation-plan.pdf (playbook excerpt). For audit purposes we also included a CloudTrail sample showing Decrypt events and the associated principal and requestId.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Redwood-KMS-Evidence
DocuSign (evidence transfer & NDA): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ABC-DOC-4521
